title: Enterprise client bindings intake: gating criteria and lifecycle rubric for language SDKs, auth, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Intake ticket to codify a repeatable gating and lifecycle rubric for enterprise SDK & client binding requests. Focus areas: language support prioritization, recommended auth patterns (token rotation, short-lived creds, KMS integrations), and streaming ergonomics (resumable sessions, backpressure semantics, handshake patterns). Goal: produce a prioritization matrix + acceptance checklist and a lightweight delivery path (prototype -> beta -> GA) that can be applied to incoming customer asks and partner integrations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A scoring rubric (weights + sample scoring) that yields a ranked backlog of SDK requests. 2) A concise guideline doc with recommended auth patterns and streaming handshakes for first-class SDKs. 3) An initial backlog of top-6 language/runtime requests with owner and prototype plan. 4) Stakeholder sign-off from Security, Developer Experience, and Sales Ops.
scoring_rubric: Weights: enterprise_signal=30, active_usage_estimate=20, engineering_effort=15, security_complexity=20, support_cost=10, strategic_fit=5. Example: Customer request from FinCorp (large private deployment) scored 85 -> high-priority. Engineering_effort uses T-shirt sizing mapped to points (S=5, M=13, L=40).
language_considerations: Call out idiomatic client surface for each language: Go (context and channels for cancellation, native goroutine-safe streaming), Java (CompletableFuture / reactive streams), Python (asyncio & sync wrappers), .NET (IAsyncEnumerable), Node (streams & event emitters). Avoid one-size-fits-all streaming API; recommend an 'adapter' pattern in core SDK to expose idiomatic interfaces per language.
auth_patterns_summary: Recommend patterns: 1) short-lived service tokens + refresh handshake (recommended for private deployments). 2) rotation-friendly SDK helpers (built-in refresh and exponential backoff). 3) explicit guidance for KMS/HSM integrations in Private mode; include sample Env var and AWS/GCP/Azure snippets. 4) Telemetry hooks to surface token refresh failures to console dashboards.
streaming_ergonomics_guidelines: Key behaviors to standardize: a) resumable sessions: checkpointed stream ids with opaque cursor; b) backpressure: client-side pull-based default with server hints; c) handshake: explicit protocol for auth check + negotiated format (json-lines vs proto); d) token rotation mid-stream: SDK must transparently refresh without losing KV cache state in runtime where possible.
operational_requirements: Minimum: automated e2e test harness for streaming scenarios, CI runners exercising token rotation flows, and a perf checklist (latency regression <10% vs baseline). Require a small canary cohort for GA (customers with low-risk integration) and rollback plan.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: inconsistent language APIs increase support burden. Mitigation: design a minimal core protocol with language adapters and shared e2e tests. Risk: token refresh failures mid-stream. Mitigation: require SDKs to implement preflight refresh and expose hooks for observability.
notes: Stakeholder inputs from Sales (customer urgency), Security (KMS requirements), DX (API ergonomics), and Eng (estimated effort). Prototype recommended: build Python & Node minimal adapters covering resumable streams + token refresh to validate design before expanding languages.

Align on scoring rubric weights with Sales & Support (this cycle)
Create e2e CI tests for token rotation and mid-stream refresh
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (spike): 1 week to validate protocol. Phase 1 (prototype): 2 sprints to ship Python+Node. Phase 2 (beta): onboard 2 enterprise pilots and collect telemetry. Phase 3 (GA): expand to top-3 additional languages with monitoring and support runbook.
decision_records: DR-2025-11-12: Adopt adapter pattern + explicit handshake for streaming. DR-2025-11-12: Prioritize security-compliant refresh flows over minimal-latency tradeoff for Private deployments.
communication: Plan to present findings at Platform Weekly (2025-11-18) and publish a short 'SDK intake rubric' doc to Confluence post-spike.
estimated_cost_notes: Rough estimate: prototype + DX work ~ 3 engineer-sprints + 1 DX sprint. Security review and integration with KMS may add +2 sprints depending on infra work.
customer_feedback_summary: FinCorp: requires resumable streams + HSM-backed keys. Acme: needs Node + Python client ergonomic improvements for streaming and token rotation. Multiple mid-market customers prefer official SDKs for onboarding speed.
qa_criteria: Automated tests for: stream resume correctness, token refresh mid-stream, handshake negotiation failures, and language-specific cancellation semantics.
open_questions: 1) Should SDK repo be monorepo or language-specific repos? 2) What level of binary compatibility support do we commit to for GA? 3) How aggressive should automated telemetry be for privacy-conscious customers?
audit_trail: Created 2025-11-04 by Maya Chen. Updated 2025-11-12 with DX and Security feedback; added prototype owners and sub-issues.
notes_for_engineering: Provide a minimal core protocol spec (one page) and a small internal test harness that can be run in CI. Prioritize building a transparent token-refresh hook early to avoid rework.
long_term_considerations: Consider building a lightweight language-agnostic streaming protocol (binary) for high-throughput use cases; evaluate tradeoffs with JSON-lines for observability and ease of debugging.
final_remark: This ticket is intended to be a reusable intake pattern: once the rubric and adapter pattern land, future SDK requests should be triaged against this checklist to accelerate delivery and reduce churn.
